mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP above its 6-month moving average signals an expansion in economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDP growth above its 6-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 10% signals a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the unemployment rate is above 10% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production above its 3-month moving average signals an expansion in economic supply, leading to increased productivity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of industrial production growth above its 3-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and retail sales above their respective 6-month moving averages signals a strong expansion in economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of joint growth in housing starts and retail sales above their respective 6-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 0.5% and an increase in the consumer price index above 2% signals an inflationary monetary easing cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 0.5% and the consumer price index is above 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 5% and an increase in payroll employment above its 3-month moving average signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of joint growth in payroll employment and decline in unemployment rate below 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in industrial production and GDP above their respective 6-month moving averages signals a strong expansion in economic supply, leading to increased productivity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of joint growth in industrial production and GDP above their respective 6-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).
